rv.q: Uneven drama examines themes of abuse, complicity and resilience from the perspective of interned historian Hannah Arendt

For all the play's arm's length approach to the dread word relatability, and the gnawing sense that there are more interesting experiences to relate just out of sight, its relevance in London, right now, could hardly be greater.
Pascal achieves nuance for the most part, allowing space for contradictions to be true at the same time without lecturing.

Drawing on archival research, Julia Pascal's The Banality of Evil: Hannah Arendt, France, 1940 explores their experiences of imprisonment and survival. However, despite the richness of its historical material, the production raises considerably more questions than it manages to explore.
